analysis.title: Aftershock: Anthropic IPO Investors Mark Valuation Down To $1.5 Trillion As Growth Slowdown Sinks In
key_insights: Per a Reuters report after Thursday's close (Oct 15), some current Anthropic investors and prospective buyers in the November IPO are weighing a valuation of around $1.5T, down from the roughly $2T previously expected. Three Reuters sources cited it, and it was attributed to attendees of Wednesday's investor day in San Francisco.

Anthropic told prospective IPO investors that Q3 revenue rose 45% sequentially to $16.8B and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis. Q2 revenue was $11.6B, more than double Q1, so investors were disappointed by the slower sequential growth rate.

ZeroHedge estimates the September exit run rate at $69B-$74B. That implies monthly growth slowed from about 33% in January-July to 3.4%-6.6% in August-September. At that pace the year ends near $89B, short of the 'more than $100B' the Street had penciled in. Hitting $100B needs Q4 growth to roughly double the Aug-Sep pace.

Goldman's Asia desk called Q3 revenue 'a big miss'. $16.8B for the quarter compares with a $5.4B implied monthly run rate for July (reported in August), implying close to zero growth in August and September. It said this weighed heavily on Asian tech sentiment, with funding stress at CoreWeave and the neocloud group adding to concerns.
Asian markets sold off on Thursday: Kospi fell nearly 8% into a bear market and tripped circuit breakers, Nikkei fell almost 5%, and Taiwan saw a record outflow of about $9.3B in foreign money.

Goldman's APAC custom baskets desk said Anthropic missed Street expectations (~$70B vs a $100B bull case) days after OpenAI's ARR reversal, and that a hot CPI made it worse. The desk had one of its busiest days, with flow about 4.5x the YTD run rate and the pad closing 4.3x better to sell. It said fundamentals mattered little against crowded positioning, leverage flushout and forced selling.

Goldman's Edoardo Greco cited Anthropic revenue growth and the focus on credit markets and neoclouds as reasons global fundamental long/short funds are down 2% month-to-date. Hedge funds sold AI stocks at the second-fastest pace in a year.

At $2T, Anthropic would trade at about 30x annualized Q3 revenue and 27x the implied September exit run rate. At $1.5T those drop to 22x and 20x, and about 17x on the $89B December run rate. The revenue is on a gross basis, which flatters the top line relative to OpenAI's net reporting.

$1.5T is still about 55% above the $965B post-money of the May round. Q4 has to deliver the reacceleration with token prices at record lows, Google and Meta crowding the frontier, and 83% of revenue from metered consumption customers can cut quickly.

Polymarket odds that Anthropic lists at $2T or more fell from 46% on Monday to 25% by Thursday evening. Odds of a valuation below $1.75T nearly tripled to 23%. The odds of a listing by Nov 30 fell to about 57% from about 69% a week earlier.
Bloomberg reported Anthropic could begin formally marketing the deal as soon as the week of Nov 9. A public S-1 is due around Oct 25 and a roadshow in early November.

The Hyperliquid Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual (io:ANTH) rallied about 6.6% from an overnight low of 1,925 to 2,053 before 5pm Thursday. It then fell as much as 9.8% to 1,851 after the Reuters headline and settled near 1,930, about 9% below a week earlier, on more than $25M daily volume.

The IPO window shows cracks: SB Energy delayed its listing, and Holtec and Firmus pulled theirs. CoreWeave shares and bonds fell again, with its 2032 bonds below 78 cents on the dollar and CDS pricing better-than-even default odds. Gartner predicts over 80% of neoclouds will fold. Jensen Huang's reassurance helped pull the Nasdaq off its lows.

Anthropic has at least $518B of compute commitments over the next decade, about 80% non-cancelable, and a $60B Broadcom chip-financing package syndicating at the same time. Each $100B cut to the valuation means more dilution for the same cash raised.

ZeroHedge's view is that $1.5T is closer to the ceiling than the floor, especially if OpenAI's next update or another CoreWeave headline lands during the roadshow. A hedge fund CIO quoted by Bear Traps said frontier models cannot support their valuations and capex, and cited a ~$68B run rate against the $80B he wanted.

earnings_insights: Anthropic (private) Q3 revenue was $16.8B, company-reported to prospective IPO investors, up 45% sequentially from $11.6B in Q2. The company said it was profitable on an adjusted basis, and a headline put Q3 gross margin at 85% (unconfirmed, per ZeroHedge). Revenue is on a gross basis, not comparable to OpenAI's net reporting.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 revenue of $16.8B, up 45% sequentially, adjusted profitability and a reported 85% gross margin got Anthropic to the table. $1.5T is still about 55% above the May round's $965B post-money, so early backers do well.
tension_points.bear_case: Sequential growth fell from over 100% in Q2 to 45% in Q3. ZeroHedge estimates monthly growth of 3.4%-6.6% in Aug-Sep, and Goldman reads close to zero. The company carries $518B of compute commitments, 83% of revenue is cuttable metered consumption, and the discounted price is still about 17x the implied December run rate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Q4 reacceleration that roughly doubles the Aug-Sep growth pace to reach the $100B year-end run rate. ZeroHedge adds that an S-1 around Oct 25 could show a number that 'reattaches the right tail'.
